newsitem.title: FINLAND: M-SERLA HAS NO TISSUE UNIT SALE PLAN - CEO.
newsitem.headline: M-SERLA HAS NO TISSUE UNIT SALE PLAN - CEO.

text.p: Metsa-Serla Oy has no immediate plans to sell its tissue business despite a decision to focus on packaging, printing and pulp, CEO Jorma Vaajoki said.
"We currently have no plans to sell that business," Vaajoki told Reuters in a telehpone interview, asked to comment on the future position of its non-core tissue operation.

Metsa-Serla said in October it would focus on core businesses -- packaging, printing and pulp -- and it on Wednesday announced the sale of its chemicals operations to Swedish Industri Kapital for 1.05 billion markka.
The tissue business is a profitable unit, and a market leader in Scandinavia, he said.
It is also much bigger in terms of net sales than the chemicals operation to be sold which has net sales of about 700 million markka, he said.
Its net sales are about two billion markka or about 15 percent of Metsa-Serla's 13.1 billion markka net sales in 1995, Vaajoki said.

Vaajoki confirmed that Metsa-Serla will book a "significant" profit from the sale of its chemicals business and said this "will not be tens but hundreds of millions of markka". He declined to elaborate.

Metsa-Serla will keep a 20 percent stake in the company that will take over its chemicals operations since it will be a raw materials purchaser for Metsa-Serla's pulp operations and a raw material supplier for its paper industry, Vaajoki said.
He also expected an increase in value for the stake.

Metsa-Serla's sawmills -- another none-core business -- will be transferred to its parent company Metsaliitto's saw mill unit Oy Metsa Timber Ltd according to a decision made earlier, Vaajoki said. He did not give any schedule for the transfer.
